source_documents.title: A Systematic Study of Auxochrome Effects on Fluorescence Under Conditions of Varying Temperature, pH, or Viscosity: Photo‐induced electron transfer and Twisted Intramolecular Charge Transfer

reference_evidence_units.quote: Thus, PET-enabled B series compounds gave less intense fluorescence than their A analogs without this pathway; likewise TICT-enabled auxochromes (C, F) gave fluorophores with lower fluorescence than those where TICT was suppressed (A, D, E, H).
reference_evidence_units.subject: series 1 (A, B, F, G)

reference_evidence_units.quote: The quantum yields of G series compounds, where both TICT and PET can operate, were lower than those from the compounds with access to only one of these quenching pathways (B, F), indicating that both deactivation mechanisms contribute to fluorescence quenching in the same sample.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1G
reference_evidence_units.statement: With N-methylpiperazine both PET and TICT quench.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Consistently, we observed a significant decrease in fluorescence intensity from PET-enabled 1B on increasing the temperature from 5 to 60 °C in MeCN and a much smaller decrease from its control 1A (Figure 2).
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1B vs 1A
reference_evidence_units.statement: PET quenching of 1B grows with temperature; 1A barely changes.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The decrease in fluorescence from 1G can therefore be attributed to increased activation of the PET channel.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1G
reference_evidence_units.statement: The temperature drop of 1G is PET, since TICT stays constant in this series.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In the PET-enabled B series, fluorescence intensity reliably increased with viscosity.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1B
reference_evidence_units.statement: Viscosity raises the emission of the PET-enabled compounds.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Increasing viscosity probably retards the fold ing necessary for the molecules to attain the correct conformation for PET to occur.
reference_evidence_units.subject: B series
reference_evidence_units.statement: Viscosity slows the folding of the pendant amine that PET needs.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Hedged ('probably'); H-bonding by glycerol not excluded.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Therefore, the fluorescence enhancement seen with 2G results from suppression of PET while that from 1G and 3G can likely be attributed to suppression of a combination of both PET and TICT.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1G
reference_evidence_units.statement: Viscosity suppresses both PET and TICT in 1G.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Third, we have confirmed that acidic conditions that protonate a pendant nitrogen block PET and so increase fluorescence while TICT is largely unaffected by pH changes as the aniline-type nitrogens are not basic enough to be protonated except at quite extreme values.
reference_evidence_units.subject: B and G series
reference_evidence_units.statement: Protonating the pendant amine blocks PET and raises fluorescence.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Viscosity enhancement assigned to suppression of both PET and TICT (restricted twisting/folding).

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: TICT by N-Caryl twisting of the piperazine also quenches; φ 0.03 is lower than with either pathway alone.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: PET from the distal piperazine N; the temperature-dependent loss of emission is assigned to PET.
